thread_analysis.thread_summary: Internal [COMPANY] staff work through two separate technical issues for [COMPANY]'s test setup. The first half covers wiring and configuration for connecting an external PC to InterLab's Automation Explore tool via a USB-Serial converter cable and cross cable, to drive DTM mode commands over a virtual COM port at a specific baud rate. The second half investigates a discrepancy where the DUT's HCI command interface reports Enhanced Power Control (EPC) as supported, but the InterLab RF Test System's actual certification test sees the DUT respond 'Not Supported' over the air during the RF/TRM/CA Enhanced Power Control test item, aborting that test -- with a recommendation to escalate the contradiction to the chipset vendor for guidance.
all_questions_found: Which COM port is the actual DUT connected to for the virtual-COM-port test setup?
Is the USB-Serial converter cable's RS232C side actually connected to the external PC, since without that connection the external PC cannot recognize the virtual COM port?
If the USB-Serial converter cable isn't connected to the external PC's USB port, would that explain the COM4 Open ERROR and COM4 access-denied errors being seen?
After the DTM-mode-entry app is confirmed working, what Automation Explore settings (COM port, baud rate, interface selection) should be used to verify RF PHY command communication is working?

If HCI-command-level interrogation shows the DUT supports Enhanced Power Control, why does the InterLab RF Test System's actual certification test report the DUT as not supporting it, aborting the RF/TRM/CA Enhanced Power Control test item?
Does Enhanced Power Control becoming active in real device-to-device operation depend on both devices supporting it, and is that relevant to the certification test result?
What information should be sent to the chipset vendor to get guidance on resolving the HCI-vs-RF-test-system Enhanced Power Control support discrepancy?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The thread covers the physical/configuration prerequisites for an external PC to communicate with a DUT via InterLab's Automation Explore over a virtual COM port (USB-Serial converter cable to the external PC's USB port, a cross cable, correct COM port and baud rate settings, and HCI-Serial interface selection), and separately, the mechanics of how the InterLab RF Test System executions a test item: it sends control commands to the DUT via the antenna signal measurement port, with each test item's initial command checking feature support before proceeding -- explaining why a DUT that reports support over HCI can still be seen as unsupported by the RF-level certification test if it responds 'Not Supported' over the air during that initial check.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: For the COM port/cabling issue, the errors observed (COM4 Open ERROR, COM4 access denied) are explained directly by the missing physical connection (USB-Serial converter cable not connected to the external PC's USB port) rather than a software or DUT problem, so the fix is to complete the cabling once the cross cable is available. For the Enhanced Power Control discrepancy, HCI-level support indication and actual RF-level certification-test behavior are evaluated differently: the certification tester's RF/TRM/CA test item begins with its own support-check command sent over the air, and if the DUT's DUT-mode response to that specific command indicates non-support, the test item is aborted regardless of what the HCI interface separately reports -- this is a genuine behavioral discrepancy in the DUT/chipset under DUT mode rather than a certification-test artifact, warranting escalation to the chipset vendor.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Misdiagnosing the COM port errors as a DUT or software problem rather than a missing cable connection would waste troubleshooting effort. Assuming the HCI-reported Enhanced Power Control support is authoritative and ignoring the RF Test System's 'Not Supported' response would risk submitting the product for the RF/TRM/CA Enhanced Power Control test item without first resolving the underlying DUT-mode behavior discrepancy with the chipset vendor, risking a repeat test failure.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When a DUT's HCI-level feature support report disagrees with its behavior during an actual certification test item, treat the certification test's own support-check response (sent and received over the air, in DUT mode) as the operative signal for that test item, and escalate the discrepancy to the chipset vendor with the specific contradiction (HCI says YES, RF test system logs 'does not support') rather than assuming either result alone settles the question.
